title: KillsValue counts the opponent's kills, and on RA2 our own deaths, as our kills
description: HandleEntityKilledByUs adds the victim's cost to cumulativeKillsValue without checking `evt.Owner == snapshot.Self`. In the sim, Destroy emits EntityKilledByUs with Owner = killer. IsEventForPlayer also delivers that event to the victim's owner when the position is visible, which it always is when our own unit dies in our own region. So each of our losses is counted as both a loss and a kill. On RA2, Ra2ObservationAssembler maps every `game.unit.killed` to EntityKilledByUs with Owner = the victim's owner. Our dead units therefore count as kills and never as losses, because HandleEntityDestroyed only handles EntityDestroyed. MinerLost, McvLost and BuildingLost never fire. Army.KillsValue and LossesValue go to the strategist, the prompt and the bandit feature vector.
failure_scenario: Sim, TwinValley, 600 s, seeds 1, 2 and 3: the arm received 36 to 38 EntityKilledByUs events owned by the opponent. The final KillsValue feature was 17200, 17400 and 17200, against true values killed by the arm of 8400, 8400 and 8000, roughly 2x. Unit test: an own E1 destroyed with events EntityDestroyed(owner self) and EntityKilledByUs(owner enemy) gives losses 200 and kills 200 (expected kills 0). RA2 path: own MTNK created, then `game.unit.killed {id}` gives kills 700 and losses 0.
suggested_fix: In HandleEntityKilledByUs, count only when `evt.Owner == snapshot.Self` and the victim is not own. In the sim, deliver EntityKilledByUs only to the killer. In the RA2 assembler, emit EntityKilledByUs only when the payload's killer is self; otherwise emit EntityDestroyed with the victim's owner.

title: IncomePerMinute estimator assumes gradual debit but the sim debits full cost up front; value is an unsmoothed per-interval spike
description: income = (credits delta over the last compile interval)/dt + current spendingRate, where spendingRate is the sum of Cost/BuildSeconds over in-progress items. The simulator (SkirmishSimulation.ApplyProduce, line 317) debits the full cost when the item is queued, and harvester unloads add CarriedValue in one lump (line 581). Credits therefore do not fall while an item builds, so the estimator reports phantom income of Cost/BuildSeconds*60 per in-progress item. Enqueue frames and harvester-dump frames produce large negative or positive spikes. There is no smoothing, so IncomePerMinute.Current and its trend deltas depend on whether a dump or an enqueue happened in the last interval. The value feeds BudgetLedger.BeginPeriod (BotRuntime.cs:235), ConditionEvaluator IncomePerMinute conditions, FeatureVector and the LLM prompt. CashRunwaySeconds divides credits by the same phantom spending.
failure_scenario: In the sim at a 1 s compile cadence, a 900-credit / 10 s tank queued at t=0 gives income of about -54000/min on the enqueue frame. For the next 10 s credits are flat, but the estimator reports +5400/min 'income' with no harvesting. When a harvester unloads 700 in one frame, income reads +42000/min for that frame and about 0 on the next. Playbook conditions such as IncomePerMinute >= X flip on single frames, and the ledger capacity swings with them.
suggested_fix: Compute income over a window from the sample ring buffer (for example, the credit delta over 15-60 s plus the integrated spending over the same window, not the instantaneous rate). Make the spending model match the source: either treat enqueue-time debits as spending events, or have the sim debit gradually like RA2. Base cash runway on windowed net burn.

title: Contact confidence rebounds upward when its last-seen region leaves sight (vacancy evidence erased)
description: Confidence is recomputed from scratch every frame as 0.5^(elapsed/halfLife). The half-life is picked from the region's visibility in the current frame only. The fast vacancy decay is not accumulated: when the region stops being visible, confidence is recomputed with the 60 s half-life over the whole elapsed time and jumps back up. This breaks the contract that confidence only decays without new evidence, and it discards the 'we looked and it's not there' evidence.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary test. An enemy tank is seen in Middle at t=0. Our rifleman keeps Middle visible t=1..30 with the tank absent, and confidence decays to 0.125. At t=31 the rifleman leaves and Middle is no longer visible, and confidence jumps to 0.699. The stale tank is then re-counted at about 70% in EnemyEstimatedArmyValue, in threat EnemyValue, and in map control (threshold 0.2), so it reappears as a threat and as Enemy control of a region we just saw empty.
suggested_fix: Decay incrementally from the previous frame's confidence: conf *= 0.5^(dt/halfLife), with halfLife chosen per interval by visibility. Or track the accumulated vacancy time separately. Confidence then never rises without a sighting.

title: A single passing enemy unit marks an ore region as Enemy (EnemyExpansionSeen), and control flicker re-fires ExpansionTaken with no de-dup
description: Map control marks a region Enemy when any non-destroyed enemy contact with confidence >= 0.2 was last seen there, including a lone scout or infantry. Contacts keep confidence >= 0.2 for about 139 s with the 60 s half-life. The ore-region transition loop then emits EnemyExpansionSeen, and later ExpansionTaken, through AddEvent with no gating, so every Own->Contested/Unknown->Own flicker re-emits 'ore region taken'. CompileMapControl also drops Enemy-controlled regions from ExpansionCandidates, so a passing scout hides our nearest expansion.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary test. Our harvester works the Middle ore field. It returns home, and at t=2 one enemy rifleman walks through Middle. Emitted: EnemyExpansionSeen r1 at t=2, although no enemy building exists. At t=31 the harvester returns and ExpansionTaken r1 fires again for a region we already held. The strategist receives false expansion events.
suggested_fix: Base EnemyExpansionSeen and Enemy ore control on enemy buildings (refinery or any structure), or on sustained presence, not on any contact. Base ExpansionTaken on own refinery or building presence. Route both through EmitGated, or keep an 'ever taken' set per region.

title: Every non-self owner is an enemy: neutral, civilian or allied entities become enemy contacts, contest our base and create a base threat
description: BeliefModel treats any entity with Owner != frame.Self as an enemy contact and as an EnemyPlayerBelief. The RA2 telemetry contract (Ra2BotTelemetryContract lines 22-26) passes through every visible entity whose owner is not the controlled player, and nothing in the contracts separates enemies from the neutral/civilian house or from allies. An unknown type resolves to Support/Vehicle/value 0, and Support is in CombatRoles, so a civilian object also counts as a threatening army contact.

The base ThreatAssessment has EnemyEtaSeconds=0 (an enemy is at the base) with EnemyValue=0. On real RA2 maps, civilian buildings, tech structures and allied units near the base or ore fields all trigger this. Tech buildings are in rulesmd as Building kind, so KnownEnemyBaseRegion and SuspectedStart can also target them.

title: SuspectedStart becomes our own base (or any lower-id start) once an enemy building is seen there
description: enemyBuildingStartRegions collects every start region where any enemy building was ever seen, and it is never pruned. The direct start is then the lowest region id in that set. A tower rush or engineer capture in our start region, or an expansion into another empty start, replaces the real enemy start whenever that region has a lower id. Our own start region is not excluded.

suggested_fix: Exclude ownStartRegions when recording enemy start regions. Choose the start by evidence (the first-seen region, or the one with the most or highest-value enemy buildings, ideally a construction yard) instead of the minimum id, and drop regions whose buildings are all confirmed destroyed.

title: Enemy units standing on a shore map to the water region and are dropped from every threat assessment
description: A contact's LastSeenRegion comes from MapInfo.RegionOf, which picks the nearest region centre, so a ground unit near a river or lake centre lands in the water region. RegionGraph uses ground links only, so Distance(waterRegion, base) is infinity and the contact never passes the ThreatSearchCells filter. Naval units and aircraft over water are dropped the same way, so their EnemyValue and ETA are never counted.
failure_scenario: Scratch test: bank region r0 is centred at (42,50) with our conyard at (40,50). A water region r1 is centred at (50,50) and linked to r0 by a naval link only. A visible enemy tank (cost 900) stands at (47,50), 7 cells from the conyard. It maps to r1, and the base threat is EnemyValue=0, EnemyEtaSeconds=9999, LocalForceRatio=10, so the base looks safe. The planner's own comment in OperationalPlanner.Squads.cs (line 274) says shore contacts map to water regions.
suggested_fix: For threats, measure distance from the contact's actual cell to the region (or use the nearest ground-reachable region for ground units). Count naval and air contacts with an any-link or straight-line distance and a suitable speed, instead of the ground-only graph.

title: ImportantUnknowns is empty for any enemy never seen, so a fully unscouted match reports no unknowns
description: The 'start unscouted', 'army not seen' and 'tech unknown' unknowns are generated only for entries in snapshot.EnemyPlayers. BeliefModel creates such an entry only after it has seen one of that player's entities. Before first contact the list is empty, which is exactly when these unknowns matter most.
failure_scenario: Scratch test: only our conyard in Home is visible for 300 s and no enemy is ever seen. At t=300, ImportantUnknowns=[] (coverage 0.33). The LLM prompt's importantUnknowns says nothing is unknown, and IntentComposer's scoutingPoor check gets no help from unknowns.
suggested_fix: Emit a player-agnostic unknown when no enemy start is known and the grace period has passed, for example 'enemy start unscouted' when no EnemyPlayerBelief has a SuspectedStart. title: CashRunwaySeconds ignores income: it reports a short runway while credits are rising
description: Runway is computed as Credits / spendingPerSecond, even though the compiler has an income estimate for the same frame. The proposal names cash runway as a deciding quantity, and the prompt passes it to the strategist. With positive net income the bank never runs out, but the feature still reports a finite and possibly short runway.
failure_scenario: Scratch test: credits rise by 50 per second while one rifleman builds (spending 10/s). Income is estimated at 3600/min against spending of 600/min, yet at t=30 (credits 2500) CashRunwaySeconds=250. A frame with 200 credits and the same queue would report 20 s of runway while the bank is growing.
suggested_fix: Use the net burn: runway = credits / max(0, spending - smoothedIncome), capped at 9999 when net burn <= 0. Use a smoothed income (for example the 15 s trend mean), not the one-frame value.
